Label: Dhanteras
Hook: Tonight we buy a little gold, or a new steel pot, for luck.
Sub: This year, add one thing that costs nothing: look at your money with attention.
Does: Luck can't be planned.
Attention can start tonight.
What you look at, you start to look after.
Line: I give my money attention, and it grows in my care.
LineHi: मेरा ध्यान मेरे धन की देखभाल करता है।
ActHead: Write three numbers on paper.
ActBody: What came in last month, what went out, what is left. Real figures. No judging.
Question: What did your family buy on Dhanteras when you were a child?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Money is just dirt on your hands. It was meant to keep us humble. Your bank balance heard it too.
Does: It makes saving feel greedy.
It makes asking for a raise feel shameful.
It makes the money leave before the 20th.
Line: I can respect money and still stay humble.
LineHi: पैसे का सम्मान और विनम्रता, दोनों मेरे साथ हैं।
ActHead: Open your UPI history for this week.
ActBody: Find one spend you didn't enjoy. Don't fix it, don't judge it. Just notice it. Noticing is where respect starts.
Question: Who in your family used to say this?

Label: Diwali
Hook: We clean every corner so Lakshmi feels welcome.
Sub: Your money has corners too: the forgotten subscription, the account you never check.
Does: Small leaks hide behind big festivals.
Unopened statements turn into quiet worry.
A clean money life feels lighter to look at.
Line: I welcome wealth into a clean, clear home.
LineHi: साफ़ और सुलझे घर में धन का स्वागत है।
ActHead: Cancel one subscription you forgot about.
ActBody: Check your UPI autopay list or card statement. One is enough for tonight.
Question: Which money corner needs cleaning this Diwali?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Wealth is restless and never stays. We say it after every bonus that vanished.
Does: It makes losing money feel like fate.
It makes a plan feel pointless.
It turns every windfall into a spending spree.
Line: Money stays longer where it has a plan.
LineHi: जहाँ योजना है, वहाँ धन टिकता है।
ActHead: Give your next salary a job before it arrives.
ActBody: Split it on paper into needs, savings and joy. Three lines are enough.
Question: Have you heard this said after money disappeared?

Label: Salary day
Hook: Credited on the 1st. Gone by the 20th.
Sub: No big purchase. Just a hundred small taps on UPI.
Does: Small spends don't feel like spending.
The balance falls without a single decision.
By month-end, worry fills the gap.
Line: Every rupee I earn finds its purpose.
LineHi: मेरी कमाई का हर रुपया अपना काम जानता है।
ActHead: Move a fixed amount aside on salary day.
ActBody: Before any spend. Even ₹500. The habit matters more than the amount.
Question: Which day of the month does your salary usually run out?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Hook: “Jitni chadar ho, utne hi pair phailao.”
HookHi: जितनी चादर हो, उतने ही पैर फैलाओ।
Sub: Stretch your legs only as far as your sheet. Good advice, but only half of it.
Does: Right: don't spend beyond what you have.
Left out: you can also grow the sheet.
Living small forever isn't the only safe choice.
Line: I live within my means, and I grow my means.
LineHi: चादर में रहना और चादर बढ़ाना, दोनों मेरे हाथ में हैं।
ActHead: Write one skill that could raise your income.
ActBody: Not a dream. One skill, and the first free step to learn it.
Question: Right now, is your sheet too small or are your legs too long?

Label: The costliest question
Sub: The most expensive question in Indian families.
Does: It doubles the wedding budget.
It buys the bigger car for the neighbours.
It keeps loans running long after the photos.
Line: I spend for my life, not for an audience.
LineHi: मेरा खर्च मेरी ज़िंदगी के लिए है, दिखावे के लिए नहीं।
ActHead: Name one spend you made mainly for others to see.
ActBody: Just name it. Seeing it clearly is how the next one gets smaller.
Question: What's one thing you bought because of log kya kahenge?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: What's at home is never valued. That includes your own work.
DoesLabel: Where it shows up at work
Does: You do extra and call it “nothing much”.
You price your work low to seem polite.
People notice your value only after you leave.
Line: I see my own value clearly, and I say it.
LineHi: अपनी क़ीमत मुझे साफ़ दिखती है, और उसे कहना मेरा हक़ है।
ActHead: List three things you did this month that saved someone time or money.
ActBody: Keep the list. It's your appraisal script.
Question: Where in your life are you the ghar ki murgi?

Label: Family and money
Sub: A loan is the scissors of love. Every family has a story.
DoesLabel: Why lending to family gets messy
Does: Nobody says the amount or the date out loud.
Asking for it back feels like an insult.
The money and the relationship both go quiet.
Line: I can love my family and protect my savings.
LineHi: परिवार से प्यार और अपनी बचत की हिफ़ाज़त, दोनों साथ चल सकते हैं।
ActHead: Decide your family-help limit before anyone asks.
ActBody: A number you can give without needing it back. Above that, you say no kindly.
Question: Have you ever lost money, or a friendship, to udhaar?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Money saved is money earned. Our grandparents lived by it.
Does: A rupee saved needs no boss and no overtime.
Savings turn emergencies into inconveniences.
A small cushion makes you braver at work.
Line: My savings give me calm and courage.
LineHi: मेरी बचत मुझे सुकून भी देती है और हिम्मत भी।
ActHead: Pick one regular spend and cut it by half this week.
ActBody: Not to zero, just half. Put the difference aside and watch it.
Question: What did your grandparents save on that you still do?

Label: Appraisal season
Hook: Your manager asks, “What are you expecting?”
Sub: And you say, “Whatever you think is fair.”
Does: It hands your number to someone else.
It signals you haven't thought about your worth.
The gap repeats every year after.
Line: I can say my number calmly.
LineHi: अपनी माँग शांति से रखना मुझे आता है।
ActHead: Find the market range for your role.
ActBody: Ask two people in your field, or read ten job posts. Write the range down.
Question: Have you ever named your number in an appraisal?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Drop by drop, an ocean fills. The oldest money lesson we have.
Does: ₹100 a day feels like nothing.
It is ₹36,500 a year.
The habit grows before the number does.
Line: Small steady steps build my wealth.
LineHi: छोटे पर लगातार क़दम मेरा धन बनाते हैं।
ActHead: Pick a daily amount you can set aside without pain.
ActBody: ₹50 or ₹100. Start tomorrow. Doing it every day is the whole trick.
Question: What will your daily boond be?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Something's off. Say it whenever a money offer sounds too good.
Does: “Guaranteed” returns, and fast.
Pressure to decide today.
A friend earns only if you join.
Line: I stay calm when an offer sounds too good.
LineHi: बहुत अच्छे लगने वाले ऑफ़र के सामने भी मेरा मन शांत रहता है।
ActHead: Don't decide on any money offer tonight.
ActBody: Sleep on every one. A real opportunity will still be there tomorrow.
Question: Have you or someone you know been caught by a too-good scheme?

Label: Kabir
Hook: “Kaal kare so aaj kar, aaj kare so ab.”
HookHi: काल करे सो आज कर, आज करे सो अब।
Sub: Do tomorrow's work today, and today's work now.
Does: The bill you avoid opening keeps growing.
The form you'll fill “next week” stays blank.
Worry runs in the background all month.
Line: I handle money tasks now, not later.
LineHi: पैसे का काम आज और अभी, कल पर नहीं।
ActHead: Do one money task you've been avoiding.
ActBody: Under ten minutes. Pay one bill, check one statement, or add one nominee.
Question: Which money task have you been putting off?

Label: A saying we grew up with
HookHi: मुफ़्त का चंदन, घिस मेरे नंदन।
Sub: Free sandalwood gets rubbed away. What costs nothing, we waste.
Does: Free delivery makes you add things you didn't need.
Free trials quietly turn into paid plans.
Cashback makes you spend in order to save.
Line: I buy what I need, not what's on offer.
LineHi: मेरी ख़रीद मेरी ज़रूरत से तय होती है, ऑफ़र से नहीं।
ActHead: Move one shopping app off your home screen.
ActBody: Just for a week. Notice how often your thumb goes looking for it.
Question: Which “free” offer tempts you most?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Greed is a curse. Every childhood story ended with this line.
Does: “Double your money in a month.”
Copying a trade from a reel.
Borrowing to chase what others made.
Line: I grow my money patiently.
LineHi: धीरज से धन बढ़ता है, और मुझमें धीरज है।
ActHead: Unfollow one account that promises fast money.
ActBody: Your feed shapes your patience. Make it a calmer place.
Question: What's the fastest-money promise you've seen this month?

Label: Family and money
Hook: You're the first earner, and everyone looks to you.
Sub: Pride, love and pressure, all in one bank account.
Does: You say yes before checking your balance.
Your own goals keep moving to “next year”.
Guilt follows every rupee you spend on yourself.
Line: Caring for my family includes caring for myself.
LineHi: परिवार की देखभाल में अपनी देखभाल भी शामिल है।
ActHead: Write one goal that is only for you.
ActBody: A course, a trip, a cushion. Give it a small monthly amount.
Question: Are you the main earner in your family?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Your own hands are your god. What you do yourself gets done.
Does: Nobody else will track your spending.
Nobody else will ask for your raise.
Small habits you build beat big promises.
Line: My own hands build my security.
LineHi: मेरी सुरक्षा मेरे अपने हाथों से बनती है।
ActHead: Set a weekly 15-minute money date with yourself.
ActBody: Same day, same time. Check your balance, your spends and one goal.
Question: Which day works for your money date?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Hook: “Ab pachhtaye hot kya, jab chidiya chug gayi khet.”
HookHi: अब पछताए होत क्या, जब चिड़िया चुग गई खेत।
Sub: What's the use of regret once the birds have eaten the field?
Does: The emergency fund we meant to start.
The cover we would “get later”.
The hospital bill that arrived first.
Line: I prepare today for the days I can't see.
LineHi: आज की तैयारी, कल के अनदेखे दिनों के लिए।
ActHead: Start an emergency envelope, however small.
ActBody: One place, one rule: only for real emergencies.
Question: What did an emergency once teach you about money?

Label: EMI
Sub: No-cost EMI makes everything sound small.
Does: Small monthly numbers hide big totals.
Three EMIs together become a second rent.
Next year's salary is spent before it arrives.
Line: I decide by the full price, not the monthly one.
LineHi: फ़ैसला पूरी क़ीमत देखकर, किस्त देखकर नहीं।
ActHead: Add up all your current EMIs.
ActBody: One total, one line. Put it next to your monthly salary.
Question: How many EMIs are you running right now?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Truth fears no fire. Honest work holds up.
Does: You never need to remember a lie.
Trust brings repeat work and referrals.
You sleep well on what you earned.
Line: I earn with honesty, and it lasts.
LineHi: ईमानदारी की कमाई टिकती है, और मेरी कमाई ईमानदार है।
ActHead: Thank one client, boss or customer by name.
ActBody: A short, honest message. Relationships are where income repeats.
Question: Who trusted you with work early on?

Label: Comparison
Hook: A school friend posts a new car. Your mood drops.
Sub: Their highlights against your behind-the-scenes.
Does: You feel behind in a race you never entered.
You spend to catch up.
Your own progress becomes invisible.
Line: My money grows at my own pace.
LineHi: मेरा धन मेरी अपनी रफ़्तार से बढ़ता है।
ActHead: Write how you're better off than three years ago.
ActBody: One honest line. Progress you don't measure doesn't feel real.
Question: What do you have now that you didn't three years ago?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: If there's life, there's a world. Health comes first.
DoesLabel: Why health is a money matter
Does: Every income plan assumes a working body.
One hospital week can undo a year of saving.
A tired mind makes costly choices.
Line: Caring for my health protects my wealth.
LineHi: सेहत का ख़याल ही धन की हिफ़ाज़त है।
ActHead: Do one thing today for the body that earns.
ActBody: A walk, an early night, or the check-up you keep postponing.
Question: What's your one health promise this week?

Label: Money silence
Hook: At home, money was never discussed in front of the children.
Sub: So we learned it by guessing.
Does: Money feels secret, even shameful.
We repeat habits we never chose.
We don't ask for help when we need it.
Line: I can talk about money openly and calmly.
LineHi: पैसे पर खुलकर और शांति से बात करना ठीक है।
ActHead: Ask one elder how they handled money at your age.
ActBody: Listen for one lesson to keep and one to leave behind.
Question: Was money talked about in your home?

Label: A belief we grew up with
Sub: The safest job is a government job. Many of us heard little else.
Does: Skills that people will pay for.
Savings that cover a bad year.
More than one source of income.
Line: My skills and savings keep me safe.
LineHi: मेरा हुनर और मेरी बचत, यही मेरी सुरक्षा है।
ActHead: Write down every source of income you have.
ActBody: Salary, freelance, rent, interest. Even ₹500 counts.
Question: What did your parents think was the “safe” career?

Label: Spending on yourself
Hook: You bought something for yourself. Then felt guilty all evening.
Sub: Many of us were taught that wanting is selfish.
Does: You overspend on others to balance it.
Joy money gets spent in secret.
Unplanned treats surprise your budget.
Line: Planned joy is part of a good money life.
LineHi: सोची-समझी ख़ुशी भी अच्छी आर्थिक ज़िंदगी का हिस्सा है।
ActHead: Give yourself a small monthly joy amount.
ActBody: Planned, guilt-free and yours. When it's used, it's used.
Question: What small thing would you love to buy without guilt?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: As you do, so you receive.
Does: This year's habits are next year's balance.
Careless small spends add up quietly.
So do careful small choices.
Line: Today's small choices shape my future wealth.
LineHi: आज के छोटे फ़ैसले मेरे कल का धन बनाते हैं।
ActHead: Write tomorrow's one money choice tonight.
ActBody: One line: what you'll skip, save or do.
Question: Which habit from last year shows in your money today?

Label: Saying no
Hook: A friend plans an expensive trip. You say yes, then regret it.
Sub: Saying no feels rude. Saying yes costs you for months.
Does: You fund plans you didn't choose.
Resentment grows quietly.
Your own goals wait again.
Line: I can say no kindly and keep my plans.
LineHi: प्यार से “ना” कहना और अपनी योजना पर टिके रहना, दोनों मुमकिन हैं।
ActHead: Practise one kind no.
ActBody: “That's not in my budget this month, but let's plan something soon.”
Question: What's the hardest money no you've had to say?

Label: Your numbers
Hook: Do you know what you spent last month? Roughly?
Sub: Most of us guess, and we guess low.
Does: The imagined number is scarier than the real one.
You can't fix what you can't see.
Worry fills the space the numbers should.
Line: I know my numbers, and they don't scare me.
LineHi: अपने आँकड़े मुझे पता हैं, और अब उनसे डर नहीं लगता।
ActHead: Download last month's bank statement.
ActBody: Add up the total spent. One number. That's all for tonight.
Question: Did the number surprise you?

Label: Night 30
Hook: Thirty nights of lines. What's different?
Sub: Not your bank balance yet. Maybe how you look at it.
DoesLabel: What a month of attention does
Does: You notice spends before they happen.
You say your number more easily.
Money feels less like a secret.
Line: I am becoming calm and clear with money.
LineHi: पैसे के साथ मेरा रिश्ता शांत और साफ़ हो रहा है।
ActHead: Write one change you've noticed in thirty nights.
ActBody: Keep it. You'll read it again on night ninety.
Question: What's one change you've noticed?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Earning fifty paise, spending a rupee. Our elders laughed at it. Cards made it easy.
Does: Cards spend money that hasn't arrived yet.
EMIs make big things feel small.
The gap shows up only at month-end.
Line: I spend from what has come in, not what might.
LineHi: मेरा ख़र्च आई हुई कमाई से चलता है, उम्मीद से नहीं।
ActHead: Put last month's income next to last month's spending.
ActBody: Two numbers. If spending is bigger, that's the gap. Seeing it is the first step.
Question: Which month this year did spending beat income?

Label: Wedding season
Hook: Three weddings this month. Three new outfits?
Sub: Shagun, travel, gifts, clothes. December weddings quietly eat January's salary.
Does: A new outfit for every function.
Shagun decided by what others gave.
Last-minute travel at peak prices.
Line: I celebrate others without borrowing from my future.
LineHi: दूसरों की ख़ुशी में शामिल होना, अपना कल गिरवी रखे बिना।
ActHead: Set one wedding budget for the whole season.
ActBody: Add up every invite. One total for gifts, clothes and travel. Then keep to it.
Question: How many weddings are you attending this season?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Distant drums sound sweet. Someone else's job, city or salary always seems better.
DoesLabel: What it does to money choices
Does: You chase moves that only look good from far.
You undervalue what's already working.
You compare your inside to their outside.
Line: I decide by the full picture, not the far-off sound.
LineHi: मेरा फ़ैसला पूरी तस्वीर देखकर होता है, दूर की आवाज़ सुनकर नहीं।
ActHead: Ask someone about the real costs of the life you envy.
ActBody: Rent, commute, hours, loans. The full picture is usually quieter.
Question: Whose life sounds like a sweet drum from where you stand?

Label: Too good to be true
Hook: A forward promises 3x returns in a month.
Sub: A cousin swears it works. The group is filling up fast. You have till tonight.
Does: Big returns, fast, with “no risk”.
Pressure to decide today.
Earn more by bringing in friends.
Line: When it's rushed and too good, I step back.
LineHi: जहाँ जल्दबाज़ी और बहुत बड़ा वादा हो, वहाँ से एक क़दम पीछे।
ActHead: Make a family rule: no money decision on a forward.
ActBody: Wait 48 hours and ask one person you trust who isn't in the group.
Question: Have you or someone you know lost money to a scheme like this?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Hook: “Sasta roye baar baar, mehenga roye ek baar.”
HookHi: सस्ता रोए बार-बार, महँगा रोए एक बार।
Sub: Buy cheap, cry again and again. Buy well, cry once.
DoesLabel: When it's true, and when it isn't
Does: True for shoes, mattresses and tools you use daily.
Not true when you pay just for the logo.
The test: how long and how often you'll use it.
Line: I pay for quality where it truly matters.
LineHi: जहाँ सच में ज़रूरी हो, वहाँ अच्छी चीज़ पर ख़र्च सही है।
ActHead: Think of one thing you've replaced three times.
ActBody: Next time, work out the cost per year of use. The better one may be cheaper.
Question: What cheap thing have you bought again and again?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Big shop, bland sweets. A fancy label doesn't make it better.
DoesLabel: Where we pay for the shop
Does: Café coffee at five times the cost.
The same rice in a prettier bag.
A brand name on an ordinary product.
Line: I pay for value, not for the shopfront.
LineHi: मेरा पैसा चीज़ की क़ीमत के लिए है, दुकान की चमक के लिए नहीं।
ActHead: Pick one item you always buy branded.
ActBody: Try the plain version once. If you can't tell the difference, keep the savings.
Question: Which brand do you pay extra for without thinking?

Label: Food delivery
Hook: 11 PM. Too tired to cook. Ordered again.
Sub: Each order feels small. The month's total rarely does.
Does: Fees and tips double a simple meal.
Tiredness, not hunger, places the order.
No one adds up the month.
Line: I plan for tired days, so they cost less.
LineHi: थके हुए दिनों की तैयारी पहले से, ताकि वे महँगे न पड़ें।
ActHead: Add up last month's food delivery orders.
ActBody: Open the app's order history. One total. No guilt, just the number.
Question: What's your usual late-night order?

Label: Kabir
Hook: “Saain itna deejiye, jaa mein kutumb samaay.”
HookHi: साईं इतना दीजिए, जा में कुटुम समाय।
Sub: Give me enough for my family, Kabir asked. Not more. Enough.
Does: Without a number, more never feels like enough.
Enough lets you stop comparing.
It makes money a tool, not a scoreboard.
Line: I know what enough looks like for my family.
LineHi: मेरे परिवार के लिए “काफ़ी” क्या है, यह मुझे पता है।
ActHead: Write your family's monthly “enough” number.
ActBody: Needs, a little joy, a little saving. One honest figure.
Question: What does “enough” mean in your home?

Label: Couples and money
Hook: You and your partner have never really talked about money.
Sub: Who earns, who spends, who worries. It's all there, just unsaid.
Does: Small spends turn into big fights.
One person carries all the worry.
Shared goals stay vague.
Line: We can talk about money as a team.
LineHi: पैसों की बात हम एक टीम की तरह कर सकते हैं।
ActHead: Ask one gentle question tonight.
ActBody: “What's one money thing you'd like us to do this year?” Then just listen.
Question: Who handles the money in your home?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Hook: “Haathi ke daant khaane ke aur, dikhaane ke aur.”
HookHi: हाथी के दाँत खाने के और, दिखाने के और।
Sub: One set of teeth to show, another to eat. A feed full of trips, a phone full of EMI alerts.
Does: Posting the holiday, paying for it till June.
Looking settled while feeling stretched.
Comparing your real life to their display.
Line: My real life matters more than how it looks.
LineHi: मेरी असली ज़िंदगी, दिखावे से ज़्यादा मायने रखती है।
ActHead: Mute one account that makes you want to spend.
ActBody: Just one. Notice how your wants change this week.
Question: Which kind of posts make you feel behind?

Label: Credit cards
Sub: Paying the minimum feels responsible. The rest keeps growing quietly.
Does: Interest runs on the unpaid balance.
The card feels paid, but it isn't.
New spends pile on top of old ones.
Line: I look at the full amount, not the smallest number.
LineHi: मेरी नज़र पूरी रक़म पर है, सबसे छोटे आँकड़े पर नहीं।
ActHead: Find the total due on your card statement.
ActBody: Not the minimum. The total. Write it next to what you can pay this month.
Question: Did you know the difference between minimum and total due?

Label: A saying worth keeping
HookHi: नया नौ दिन, पुराना सौ दिन।
Sub: New shines for nine days; old serves for a hundred. Your phone works fine. The ad says otherwise.
Does: The thrill fades in a week.
The payment lasts a year.
The old one still worked.
Line: I use what I have well before I replace it.
LineHi: जो पास है, उसका पूरा इस्तेमाल पहले, नया बाद में।
ActHead: Pick one thing you planned to upgrade.
ActBody: Wait 30 days and write the date down. If you still need it then, decide calmly.
Question: What's the oldest thing you own that still works perfectly?

Label: A saying worth keeping
HookHi: सब्र का फल मीठा होता है।
Sub: Patience bears sweet fruit. Money rewards it more than most things.
Does: Savings need time more than size.
Waiting a week ends most impulse buys.
Steady beats sudden, almost every time.
Line: I let good things take their time.
LineHi: अच्छी चीज़ों को समय देने का धैर्य मेरे पास है।
ActHead: Start a 7-day wait list.
ActBody: Anything you want to buy goes on it first. After 7 days, buy only what still matters.
Question: What did you once wait for that felt sweeter because of it?

Label: Ageing parents
Hook: Your parents never ask for money. But you wonder.
Sub: Their savings, their health costs, their pride. Nobody brings it up.
Does: Emergencies arrive before plans do.
Siblings assume someone else will help.
Parents struggle quietly so as not to be a burden.
Line: I care for my parents with planning, not panic.
LineHi: माता-पिता की देखभाल घबराहट से नहीं, तैयारी से।
ActHead: Find out where your parents keep their important papers.
ActBody: Bank, property, health. Ask gently, over tea. Just where, not how much.
Question: Have you ever talked to your parents about their money?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Whenever you wake up, that's your morning. It's not too late to start with money.
Does: It turns regret into doing nothing.
It compares you to people who started at 22.
It wastes the years you still have.
Line: Today is a good day to begin.
LineHi: शुरुआत के लिए आज का दिन अच्छा है।
ActHead: Do one money task you've delayed for months.
ActBody: Add a nominee, close an old account, read a statement. Just one.
Question: What money habit do you wish you'd started earlier?

Label: Sale season
Sub: The clock is the product. Most of the cart wasn't on your list.
Does: Urgency skips the question “do I need it?”
A discount on something unneeded is still a cost.
The sale comes back next month.
Line: A deadline doesn't decide my spending.
LineHi: मेरा ख़र्च किसी डेडलाइन के दबाव में तय नहीं होता।
ActHead: Empty your shopping cart tonight.
ActBody: If you still want it in three days, it will still be there, or on sale again.
Question: What's the best sale buy you never used?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Weigh your words before you speak. Weigh a purchase before you pay.
Does: How many hours of work does it cost?
How often will I really use it?
Will I be glad about it in a month?
Line: I weigh my choices before I pay.
LineHi: हर ख़र्च से पहले उसे तोलना मेरी आदत है।
ActHead: Work out what one hour of your work earns.
ActBody: Monthly take-home divided by hours worked. Use it to price your next want.
Question: What would you skip if you priced it in hours?

Label: Kids and money
Hook: A child asks, “Why can't we buy it?”
Sub: “We can't afford it” teaches fear. “It's not in this month's plan” teaches choice.
Does: Money talk at home becomes money habits later.
A plan sounds safer than a shortage.
Kids copy what we do, not what we say.
Line: Our home talks about money calmly.
LineHi: हमारे घर में पैसों की बात शांति से होती है।
ActHead: Give a child one small money choice this week.
ActBody: ₹100 for a snack or a toy, their decision. No child at home? Think back to yours.
Question: What did your parents say when you asked for things?

Label: A saying we grew up with
HookHi: चमड़ी जाए पर दमड़ी न जाए।
Sub: Lose the skin, but not a paisa. Saving taken so far it starts to hurt.
Does: Skipping the doctor to save a fee.
Missing family moments to avoid any spend.
Never enjoying what you saved for.
Line: I save with care, and I spend with care.
LineHi: बचत भी सोच-समझकर, ख़र्च भी सोच-समझकर।
ActHead: Name one thing you've been too strict to spend on.
ActBody: If it's for health or family, plan for it this month.
Question: Do you lean more towards spending or holding back?

Label: Gifting season
Hook: Gifts for everyone this week. A budget for none.
Sub: Christmas, Secret Santa, the year-end party. It adds up fast.
Does: Each gift is decided alone, never in total.
We match what others spent.
Last-minute means full price.
Line: My gifts come from care, not from pressure.
LineHi: मेरे तोहफ़े दबाव से नहीं, दिल से आते हैं।
ActHead: List everyone you'll gift, then set one total.
ActBody: Divide it fairly. A handwritten note can carry more than a price tag.
Question: What's the most meaningful gift you've received?

Label: Family and money
Sub: One pomegranate, a hundred patients. One salary, a hundred demands.
Does: Everyone's need feels urgent.
Your own needs go last.
Saying no feels selfish.
Line: I share fairly, and I keep a part for us.
LineHi: सबका ख़्याल, पर अपने हिस्से की बचत भी।
ActHead: List every demand on your salary.
ActBody: Family, EMIs, bills, help. Then put your own savings at the top of the list.
Question: How many people does your income look after?

Label: Emergencies
Hook: A hospital visit nobody planned for.
Sub: It's never convenient. The scramble for papers makes it worse.
Does: Papers found in minutes, not hours.
One calm person instead of five panicked ones.
Money decisions made clearly, not in a rush.
Line: When trouble comes, I'm ready, not rushing.
LineHi: मुश्किल आए तो घबराहट नहीं, तैयारी हो।
ActHead: Keep your family's health papers in one folder.
ActBody: IDs, reports, any policy papers. Tell one other person where it is.
Question: Could your family find your important papers tonight?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: One trip, two jobs done. Some habits save money and give something back.
Does: Walking short trips: fare saved, health gained.
Cooking at home: money saved, family time added.
Mending instead of replacing: savings and a skill.
Line: My good habits pay me twice.
LineHi: मेरी अच्छी आदतें दोहरा फ़ायदा देती हैं।
ActHead: Pick one two-in-one habit for this week.
ActBody: Walk, cook, mend or borrow. Note what it saved.
Question: Which habit saves you money and something else too?

Label: Friends and money
Hook: You ordered dal. The bill is split equally.
Sub: Speaking up feels petty. Staying quiet costs you every time.
Does: We don't want to look cheap.
We assume it evens out. It rarely does.
Small unfairness turns into quiet resentment.
Line: I can be generous and still be fair to myself.
LineHi: दरियादिली और अपने साथ इंसाफ़, दोनों साथ चल सकते हैं।
ActHead: Practise one easy line.
ActBody: “Shall we split by what we ordered? It's easier for me this month.”
Question: Do you split equally or by what you ordered?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Do good, and good returns. Giving belongs in a money plan too.
Does: Planned giving never strains the month.
It goes where you care most.
It reminds you that money is for people.
Line: I give with a glad heart and a clear plan.
LineHi: देना मेरे लिए ख़ुशी है, और उसकी भी योजना है।
ActHead: Decide a small amount to give this month.
ActBody: To a cause, a helper or a neighbour. Choose it on purpose.
Question: Who would you like to help this month?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Can't dance, so blame the crooked courtyard. Prices, salary, luck: all easy to blame.
Does: Some things really are outside our control.
Blame hides the part that is in our hands.
Small changes start where blame stops.
Line: I focus on the part that's in my hands.
LineHi: मेरा ध्यान उस हिस्से पर है जो मेरे हाथ में है।
ActHead: Write one money problem, and one part you control.
ActBody: Just one part. Even a small one. That's where tomorrow starts.
Question: Which money problem do you blame on the courtyard?

Label: Year end
Hook: The year is almost over. Where did the money go?
Sub: Not to judge. Just to look once before the calendar changes.
Does: Patterns hide inside single months.
A whole year shows what you really value.
It makes next year's plan honest.
Line: I look back with kindness and plan with care.
LineHi: पीछे मुड़कर नरमी से देखना, आगे सोच-समझकर बढ़ना।
ActHead: Write your three biggest spends of the year.
ActBody: Next to each, write: worth it, or not. Keep the list for January.
Question: What was your best money decision this year?

Label: New year
Hook: New year resolutions. Most are gone by the third week.
Sub: Big promises fade. Small habits stay.
Does: A small habit needs no motivation.
It survives busy weeks.
It grows into the big change slowly.
Line: This year, my promises are small and steady.
LineHi: इस साल वादे छोटे, पर पक्के।
ActHead: Choose one money habit for January only.
ActBody: One month. Tick a calendar every day you do it.
Question: What's your one money habit for January?

Label: A saying worth keeping
HookHi: जितना गुड़ डालोगे, उतना मीठा होगा।
Sub: The more jaggery you add, the sweeter it gets. What you put in shapes what you get.
Does: Time spent learning leads to better choices.
Regular saving builds a real cushion.
Care in your work builds trust over the years.
Line: What I put in today shapes my tomorrow.
LineHi: आज की मेहनत ही कल की मिठास है।
ActHead: Spend 20 minutes learning one money topic.
ActBody: Reading your payslip, how loan interest works, or making a budget. Just 20 minutes.
Question: Which money topic would you like to understand better?

Label: Night 60
Hook: Sixty nights. Two months of lines.
Sub: Habits take about this long to start feeling normal.
Does: The small step happens without a reminder.
Money talk feels less awkward.
You notice leaks before they open.
Line: Calm money habits are part of who I am now.
LineHi: शांत और समझदार पैसों की आदतें अब मेरी पहचान हैं।
ActHead: Read what you wrote on night 30.
ActBody: Add one more change you've noticed since then.
Question: Which night's line has stayed with you?
